about: The lint ratchet's baseline (scripts/lint.mjs, pnpm lint): Biome's violations per rule and file when the linter came in, which may only go down. A new or raised count fails, and so does a lowered one until this file is rewritten with node scripts/lint.mjs --write-baseline (the `off` reasons are kept). `off`: each rule biome.json turns off, with why its hits are the code's idiom rather than a defect.

off.lint/style/noNonNullAssertion: About 3,500 `!` after a lookup the code has just checked (maps, regex groups, test values); the type checker's strict mode is the guard.
off.lint/style/useTemplate: Style only: short concatenations read as well as templates.
off.lint/complexity/noCommaOperator: The comma in an arrow body or a loop step is a deliberate short form (`() => (clearTimeout(t), r())`).
off.lint/suspicious/noTemplateCurlyInString: `${…}` inside plain strings is shell or scenario-template text on purpose (hooks, fake tools in tests).
off.lint/suspicious/noControlCharactersInReg: The control-character patterns are the point: untrusted text is cleaned of them before it is shown.
off.lint/suspicious/useIterableCallbackRetur: `forEach((x) => set.add(x))` returns a value nobody reads; harmless.
off.lint/suspicious/noThenProperty: `then` is a domain word here (the scenario before an edit, `replanEdit({ now, then })`), never awaited.
off.lint/correctness/noChildrenProp: The Studio's tests and kit build elements with `createElement(C, { children })` on purpose.
off.lint/correctness/noVoidTypeReturn: `return v.forEach(walk)` in a void walker is a short form of a call and a return.
off.lint/correctness/noEmptyCharacterClassIn: `[^]` (any character, newlines included) is used on purpose in multi-line test patterns.
